solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dance in colossal saloon

indicators.note: 'in' tells the solver the answer sits inside the run of letters that follows

parts.note: the letters straddle the join between the two words

explanation.surface: Someone dances in a huge bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Salsa is a lively Latin American dance style, so it is one example of a dance.

clue.text: Feature of a pirate flag from racing boat, reportedly

indicators.note: 'reportedly' means as it is said out loud, so the word is chosen for its sound

parts.note: a scull is a light racing rowing boat

explanation.surface: Pirate flag imagery borrowed from a boat used in racing.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jolly Roger shows a skull above crossed bones, so the skull is a central emblem of the pirate flag.

clue.text: Fail to be swimming? This may help!

definitions.text: Fail to be swimming? This may help!

indicators.note: letters that are swimming are moving about loosely, so they are to be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, all eight letters

explanation.surface: If you can't manage to swim, here is something that will rescue you.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the rearranged letters give the thing that helps someone who cannot stay afloat.
explanation.definitionFit: A lifeboat is a rescue vessel that saves people struggling in the water, which is exactly the help the clue describes.

clue.text: Clothes from Santa regularly wear out

indicators.note: 'regularly' asks for letters taken at even intervals, here every second one

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of the word
to tire is to wear out or exhaust

explanation.surface: Father Christmas's red suit gets worn out from all those deliveries.
explanation.definitionFit: Attire is a formal word for clothing or garments.

clue.text: Stunned a mother with last letter?

parts.note: taken as written
ma is an informal word for mother
zed is the British name for Z, the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A mum is shocked by the final letter she receives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last letter' reads like a final piece of post, but it is the alphabet's last letter, called zed in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Amazed means greatly surprised, the same as stunned in its sense of astonished.

clue.text: Kerfuffle is not yet completed

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a fuss or commotion
second meaning: a task still outstanding, as on a list

explanation.surface: The fuss is still unfinished business.
explanation.definitionFit: A to-do is a fuss or commotion, and a job still to do remains unfinished, so the hyphenated phrase covers both.

clue.text: Laid back regarding head of legal getting fired

parts.note: re means concerning or regarding

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only that letter is kept

parts.note: its first letter
to be axed is to be sacked from a job

explanation.surface: Someone stays calm about the boss of the legal department being sacked.
explanation.definitionFit: Laid back is an idiom for calm and easy-going, a synonym of relaxed.

clue.text: Temple too dilapidated for native American carving

indicators.note: a dilapidated building has fallen apart, so its letters are to be rebuilt in another order

parts.note: taken as written, all nine letters

explanation.surface: A crumbling place of worship is swapped for a tribal carving.
explanation.definitionFit: Totem poles are tall wooden posts carved with emblems by Indigenous peoples of the Pacific Northwest.

clue.text: Pills split by nine playing game

indicators.note: letters that are playing are at play, moving about freely into a new arrangement
something split by another thing has that thing driven into its middle

parts.note: tablets are pills
the four letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Medicine is divided among nine people during a match.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters go in just before the final S of the pills word.
explanation.definitionFit: Table tennis, or ping-pong, is an example of a game played with bats and a light ball.

clue.text: Out of shape female entering military group

indicators.note: something entering another goes inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a unit is a body of soldiers
F is the standard abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A woman joins an army squad while not in good physical condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfit means in poor physical condition, which is what being out of shape describes.

clue.text: Novel, say, includes a Zulu with a large weapon

indicators.note: a thing that includes others holds them inside itself

parts.note: a novel is an example of a book, hence 'say'
taken as written
Zulu is Z in the NATO phonetic alphabet
taken as written

explanation.surface: A novel features a Zulu warrior carrying a big weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: The first A and the Z go inside the book after its B; the second A is tacked on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A bazooka is a shoulder-fired anti-tank rocket launcher, a hefty weapon.

clue.text: Defamation engulfs king and a politician

indicators.note: to engulf is to swallow up, so the other pieces end up inside

parts.note: libel is written defamation
R stands for rex, Latin for king
'and' joins; the A is taken as written

explanation.surface: A slander case swallows up a monarch and a member of parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: A Liberal is a member of the Liberal Party, an example of a politician.

clue.text: Back with silly red nose

indicators.note: silly suggests nonsense, so the letters are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, all seven letters

explanation.surface: Supporting a cause by wearing a comic red nose, as on Comic Relief day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' is the verb meaning support, not the rear of anything. Red Nose Day is a British charity telethon.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse a candidate or product is to back it, giving public support.

clue.text: Charity is embarrassed and angry

parts.note: someone embarrassed goes red in the face
'and' joins; cross means angry

explanation.surface: A charitable donor feels both ashamed and annoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Red Cross is a worldwide humanitarian organisation, an example of a charity.

clue.text: Word of praise about advertisement's boldness

indicators.note: 'about' here means around, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: bravo is a cry of approval
ad is short for advertisement; the 's links to the definition

explanation.surface: A critic applauds the daring of a commercial.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravado is a show of boldness or swagger, often intended to impress.

clue.text: Daily grind beginning to relent a little

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, which is all that is kept

parts.note: its first letter
a trace means a tiny amount

explanation.surface: The daily grind begins to ease off slightly.
explanation.definitionFit: The rat race is an idiom for the exhausting competitive routine of working life.

clue.text: Fear a biathlon covering hot sandy region

indicators.note: the outer words are covering the answer, holding it within them

parts.note: the letters run across all three words

explanation.surface: An athlete dreads a biathlon held somewhere scorching and sandy.
explanation.walkthrough: A biathlon is usually a winter event, which makes the desert setting comic.
explanation.definitionFit: Arabia, the peninsula in south-west Asia, is famous for its vast hot deserts.

clue.text: Joiner's plates smashed

indicators.note: smashed crockery is broken into pieces, so the letters are to be reassembled

parts.note: taken as written, all six letters

explanation.surface: A carpenter's crockery has been broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joiner' suggests a carpenter, but it means anything that fastens things together; the 's is short for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A staple fastens sheets of paper together, so it is a kind of fastener.

clue.text: Spots new section

indicators.note: something new has been made afresh, so the letters are put into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written, all seven letters

explanation.surface: Someone sees a fresh part of a document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spots' is the verb meaning sees, not the noun for marks.
explanation.definitionFit: To notice something is to observe or catch sight of it, as spots does.

clue.text: Initially settle on blue-green: a bargain!

definitions.note: the answer is a noun used with 'a': it's a steal

indicators.note: 'Initially' means at the start, so only the opening letter is wanted

parts.note: its first letter
teal is a blue-green colour

explanation.surface: A shopper decides on a blue-green item at a knock-down price.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'on' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sold so cheaply it is almost taken for free is informally called a steal.

clue.text: Scoundrel at home following football team

indicators.note: 'following' means coming after, so the piece before it in the clue is placed second

parts.note: Aston Villa is a Birmingham football club, usually called Villa
someone in is at home

explanation.surface: A rogue stays home watching the soccer side he supports.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' puts the home piece after the team, though it reads like a fan following a club.
explanation.definitionFit: A villain is a wicked person or rogue, a synonym of scoundrel.

clue.text: Record composer on the radio

indicators.note: radio is heard, not read, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: Franz Liszt was a Hungarian composer and pianist

explanation.surface: A recording by a composer is played on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record' is the verb meaning to set down in a list, not a disc.
explanation.definitionFit: To list items is to record or enter them one after another.

clue.text: Examine front of polyester garment

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter, the only one kept

parts.note: its first letter
a robe is a long loose garment

explanation.surface: Someone inspects the front of a synthetic piece of clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To probe is to investigate or examine something closely.

clue.text: Gloomy when accepting one's second sacking

indicators.note: accepting something means taking it in, so the other pieces go inside

parts.note: dismal means gloomy
one is I, so one's is I'S
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: A worker is downcast at being fired for the second time.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacking is informal for being fired from a job, which is a dismissal.

clue.text: Sly person is not opening art equipment

indicators.note: 'not opening' means without its opening letter, so the first one goes

parts.note: a weasel is a sly, untrustworthy person

explanation.surface: A crafty character refuses to open up his art supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is the stand that holds an artist's canvas, a piece of painting equipment.
